newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss franc ends firmer but pressured after Rubin.
newsitem.headline: Swiss franc ends firmer but pressured after Rubin.

text.p: 1430 GMT - The Swiss franc ended ending higher versus the dollar and mark, but the closing rates reflected a near-static market which was waiting for U.S. Treasury secretary Robert Rubin to begin speaking.
The franc ended near its highs against the dollar, after the U.S. currency dropped below 1.47 francs in late trade.
But after the close, the dollar rose back towards 1.47 francs as market focused on Rubin's comment that a strong dollar was in the U.S.'s interest.

But one trader said the dollar's late rise was a "wishy-washy move. I think there is only one thing going on, and that is a much stronger yen. Rubin didn't say anything new, the yen overall is going to strengthen," the trader said. This also applied to yen/Swiss, he said. He added that Rubin said the U.S. shared Japan's concern about a weaker yen.
* The dollar closed at 1.4674/4679 Swiss francs, compared with 1.4730/4740 francs at the close on Wednesday.
* The mark ended at 85.53/55 Swiss centimes versus 85.70/71 centimes at Wednesday's close.
